paths.description: Requested homepage and primary-content entry; redirected to the regional login/authentication gate, so the catalogue/content journey could not be exercised.
Authentication and age-gate archetype; inspected visually, structurally, with keyboard/media preferences, performance, network, security, discoverability and memory probes.
Password-recovery form archetype and recovery journey.
Primary public support/contact form, including invalid submission and recovery state.
Long-form public legal/content template used to assess reading, navigation, metadata, accessibility and responsive behavior.
Unknown-route recovery attempt; the route redirected to the login gate rather than exposing a distinct 404 recovery page.

findings.summary: The interface is hard-coded dark rather than following the user color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Light and dark emulations rendered the same black surface, the root computed color-scheme was normal, and the DOM probe found no color-scheme or prefers-color-scheme token.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare supported schemes at the root and provide preference-driven color tokens with a deliberate light and dark palette.

findings.summary: Route changes have no directional or continuity transition.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found no view-transition token and navigation between login, reset, support and privacy is a full abrupt swap.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively add same-origin cross-document View Transitions, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-state-aware navigation aid.
findings.evidence: The privacy page is over 18,000 CSS px tall in Lighthouse, while probes found no scroll-timeline or scroll-state implementation and the screenshot shows static chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight progress indicator or responsive sticky section navigation for long legal pages.

findings.summary: Navigation does not cue where focus or context moved.
findings.evidence: The public templates use full page swaps and static tab links with no view transition, highlight or post-navigation attention cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Use directional transitions and explicit current-location/focus treatment, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: The authentication gate uses an ad-hoc ARIA dialog instead of the native dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: The login DOM contains one role=dialog and zero dialog elements; the gate is fixed and has no native close/light-dismiss behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog for a genuinely modal gate, with correct focus containment and a clearly documented non-dismissable state when legally required.

findings.summary: Mobile layouts retain a 990 px desktop canvas and clip primary forms.
findings.evidence: At 360 px, layout probes measured scrollWidth 990 and 630 px horizontal overflow on both login and support. The support screenshot cuts off inputs and navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace fixed 990 px widths with intrinsic, fluid layouts and verify every primary form at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Forms and navigation do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: The support form is clipped at 360 px and the probe found no container-query tokens on reused form/navigation components.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container queries or intrinsic grid/flex sizing so labels, fields, tabs and CAPTCHA reflow within narrow containers.

findings.summary: Many interactive targets are too short for reliable touch use.
findings.evidence: The probe found many visible links only 15 to 19 px high across login, privacy and support; focus itself was visible with a 2 px outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 24 by 24 CSS px, preferably 44 px for primary mobile controls, without removing visible focus.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is slow on primary public pages.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 5.2 s on login and 4.3 s on privacy, both outside the good range; CLS remained 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency, reduce document/server delay, and prioritize the actual LCP resource while deferring non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: A long main-thread task blocks the login page.
findings.evidence: The CDP trace recorded one 554.46 ms long task and 504.46 ms total blocking time in the captured load window.
findings.suggestedFix: Attribute the long task, split or defer the responsible work, and schedule non-essential analytics after the page is interactive.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking scripts and a long dependency chain delay content.
findings.evidence: HAR signals identified three VeryHigh parser-inserted stylesheets and two synchronous head scripts; the live DOM confirmed TrafficJunky and default-default.js are in head without async, defer or module.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical head scripts, inline only truly critical CSS, and shorten the LCP dependency chain.

findings.summary: Analytics scripts dominate a simple login page payload.
findings.evidence: The login transferred 567 KB; 400 KB was script, including 298 KB from two Google Tag Manager resources, for a simple two-field login surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit tag-manager containers and remove, consolidate or conditionally load scripts that do not support the login task.

findings.summary: Accessibility semantics are invalid or missing on public templates.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found aria-required-children and listitem failures on the privacy tab list; probes also found visible controls whose accessible naming depends only on image/title or placeholder patterns.
findings.suggestedFix: Repair the tab/list semantics, use native navigation lists where possible, and give every interactive control a robust accessible name.

findings.summary: Text and controls repeatedly fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 16 contrast failures on login and 12 on privacy, including white on #ec567c at 3.39:1 and footer text at 3.17:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust brand and muted-text tokens to meet WCAG contrast in every state, and retest with axe/Lighthouse.

findings.summary: Heading, landmark and ARIA structure is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Privacy starts with H2 headings, includes an empty H4, and Lighthouse reports no main landmark plus an invalid role=tablist child structure. Keyboard focus was visible on the skip link.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide one main landmark, a logical H1-led outline, and valid tab semantics while preserving visible focus.

findings.summary: Long-form text is clipped and difficult to read on narrow screens.
findings.evidence: The 990 px fixed canvas produces 630 px overflow at 360 px; the support and legal templates require sideways navigation, while privacy text uses long dense lines on desktop.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a responsive readable measure, fluid type/spacing, and reflow all legal and form content without horizontal scrolling.

findings.summary: The viewport disables user scaling and the page fails mobile reflow.
findings.evidence: All probed pages declare user-scalable=0, and mobile layout evidence shows 630 px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=0 and ensure content reflows at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom without two-dimensional scrolling.

findings.summary: Image sizing and delivery hygiene are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The image probe found three of six images without both dimensions, three without responsive sources and five legacy-format assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width and height, responsive sources where useful, and modern formats for non-vector assets.

findings.summary: The pages are not eligible for a clean back-forward cache restore.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three BFCache failure reasons on both login and privacy.
findings.suggestedFix: Inspect the BFCache audit details, remove avoidable blockers, and preserve page state on back/forward navigation.

findings.summary: The login page has no meta description.
findings.evidence: The login probe and raw-HTML discoverability result found a descriptive title and H1 but no meta description.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, route-specific meta description for the login and recovery surfaces.

findings.summary: robots.txt is not served as a valid robots file and mobile friendliness is compromised.
findings.evidence: /robots.txt returns a 301 to /robots.txt/ and ultimately the login HTML; Lighthouse reports 913 robots errors. The viewport also disables scaling.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a plain-text robots.txt at the canonical path and remove scale restrictions from the viewport.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are internally inconsistent because robots.txt is broken.
findings.evidence: Canonical and hreflang links and sitemap.xml are present, but the canonical robots endpoint redirects away instead of returning directives.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore a valid robots.txt and verify its sitemap and crawl rules against canonical and hreflang URLs.

findings.summary: Public informational pages lack share and structured metadata.
findings.evidence: The privacy page exposes zero JSON-LD blocks and no Open Graph tags despite being a public, indexable legal entity page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph metadata and appropriate organization/web-page structured data to public information pages.

findings.summary: The login surface lacks baseline security headers and sets insecure cookies.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP and nosniff are missing. PHPSESSID and platform cookies lack Secure; all six observed cookies use SameSite=None and none are HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP and nosniff, then mark session cookies Secure, HttpOnly and with the narrowest workable SameSite policy.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party collection are disproportionate on the login gate.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe found 10 third-party origins and Google Analytics, DoubleClick and Tag Manager. HAR attributed 489 KB of 567 KB to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize login-page collection, gate optional analytics behind valid consent, and remove third parties that are not necessary for authentication.

findings.summary: Authentication exposes password-only fields with no passkey path.
findings.evidence: No permission prompt fired on load, but the login DOM contains password fields and the probe found no WebAuthn or navigator.credentials implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey authentication and recovery alongside existing methods, with password autocomplete retained as a fallback.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are absent.
findings.evidence: The main response has HSTS and X-Frame-Options, but no CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP with frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and nosniff; stage and monitor CSP before enforcement.

findings.summary: Primary controls are cut off rather than repositioning at viewport edges.
findings.evidence: At 360 px, the support select, text fields and top navigation extend beyond the viewport on a 990 px canvas.
findings.suggestedFix: Make navigation and forms intrinsically responsive so all controls stay reachable at viewport edges.

findings.summary: The installable shell has no observable offline cache.
findings.evidence: A manifest and active service worker are registered, but Cache Storage contained no caches after load, providing no evidence of an offline fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Precache a small offline fallback and test navigation with the network disabled while keeping live content online-only.

findings.summary: Unknown routes redirect to login instead of explaining the failure.
findings.evidence: A deliberately unknown URL ended at /login/ with the ordinary login page and no 404 or recovery-specific message.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an intentional 404/error state with clear links back to safe entry points instead of silently changing the destination.

findings.summary: Localized routes are advertised but layouts rely on physical CSS.
findings.evidence: Pages have lang=en and hreflang variants including Arabic, but probes found physical left/right properties and no logical-property tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical inline/block properties and verify dir=rtl rendering on the advertised Arabic locale.

findings.summary: Visible dates are hard-coded in English rather than locale-aware.
findings.evidence: The privacy page renders “April 16th, 2026” while advertising many localized variants; no locale-aware date markup or Intl-driven output was observable.
findings.suggestedFix: Render dates from unambiguous data using Intl.DateTimeFormat for each locale.

findings.summary: The login page presents conflicting account options and runs tracking before a clear consent choice.
findings.evidence: The gate states registrations are unavailable in the region while the underlying page still offers Sign Up; trackers include Analytics and DoubleClick while cookie choice is only a footer link.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unavailable calls to action for the current region and present an equally prominent, honest privacy choice before optional tracking.

findings.summary: Authentication and contact fields omit autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: Login email/password, recovery email and support fields all reported empty autocomplete values.
findings.suggestedFix: Add correct autocomplete tokens such as username, current-password, email and name where applicable.

findings.summary: Several small assets use legacy formats and lack responsive/intrinsic metadata.
findings.evidence: Five of six images are PNG/GIF, three lack complete dimensions and three lack responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Use SVG/WebP/AVIF where appropriate, provide dimensions, and avoid duplicate logo downloads.

findings.summary: The login page performs avoidable analytics work.
findings.evidence: Two Google tag resources transfer 298 KB and tracking spans 10 third-party origins on a simple authentication gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer or eliminate non-essential analytics and batch only consented measurements after the core task is ready.

findings.summary: Third parties consume most of the login transfer budget.
findings.evidence: Third-party requests account for 489 KB of 567 KB transferred, with tag-manager scripts the two largest resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party budget for authentication pages and enforce it in deployment monitoring.

taskList.title: Rebuild public templates as fluid, zoomable mobile layouts
Harden login headers and cookie attributes
Reduce authentication-page tracking and third-party script weight
Fix contrast, landmarks and ARIA semantics
Improve LCP and unblock resource delivery
Restore valid robots and metadata signals
Modernize authentication with passkeys and autofill
Adopt preference-aware theming and motion continuity
Improve semantic overlays, targets and platform hygiene
Add resilient offline and error states
Make localized templates bidi and locale aware
Optimize image assets and intrinsic dimensions
